Most menus, views and controls can be reached from the keyboard. The Navigate menu moves focus between areas of the interface and holds the Tab navigation options; more are in the Display & Input Settings.
Ableton/Live/UG/41 Accessibility and Keyboard Nav/04 Navigating in Live covers each view.

With Use Tab to Move Focus on, Tab / Shift+Tab move to the next or previous control, and Option+Tab / Option+Shift+Tab (Mac), Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab (Win) move along a row in the Session or Arrangement mixer.
With it off, Tab switches between Session and Arrangement View.
Wrap Tab Navigation — Tab past the last control returns to the first, and Shift+Tab on the first goes to the last.

Move Clips with Arrow Keys — on by default; left and right arrows move selected clips or the time selection in the Arrangement. With it off, left and right collapse the time selection to its start or end.
Same content as Ableton/Live/UG/41 Accessibility and Keyboard Nav/01 Menu and Keyboard Navigation Settings/01 Using Tab for Navigation.
42.26.2 Navigating Between Controls in the Settings Menu
Tab and Shift+Tab move between options in a Settings tab, whether or not Use Tab to Move Focus is on. Up and down arrows change a focused option; Enter flips a toggle.
42.26.2 Navigating Between Controls in the Settings Menu
Option+Tab / Option+Shift+Tab (Mac), Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab (Win), or the arrows on the focused Settings Page Chooser switch tabs. Shift+Tab from a tab's first control returns to the chooser.
42.26.2 Navigating Between Controls in the Settings Menu
42.27 Editing Automation and Modulation Envelopes with the Keyboard

Breakpoints in automation and modulation envelopes can be added, edited and deleted from the keyboard; see Ableton/Live/UG/41 Accessibility and Keyboard Nav/05 Editing Automation and Modulation Envelopes.
42.27 Editing Automation and Modulation Envelopes with the Keyboard
Mac: Cmd+? opens a search field that suggests menu entries as you type; arrows choose and Enter runs.
Windows: Alt plus a menu's first letter opens it, such as Alt+F for File. Up and down move through items, left and right open neighboring menus, and Enter chooses.
Right-click (Win) or Ctrl-click (Mac) an area of Live for its context menu. From the keyboard: VO+Shift+M (Mac), or Menu or Shift+F10 (Win).
Some context menus include options from Live's Settings; changing them affects the whole program, not just the selected item.

Some commands appear only in context menus, including browser options, grid marker commands for Auto-Warp, grid line width options, copy and paste of Operator envelopes and oscillators, and many device-specific commands.

Resumes Arrangement playback after a Session clip has taken over a track. It lights up while what plays differs from the Arrangement, and appears in both the Session View and the Arrangement View.

Jumps playback to the next locator, or the Arrangement end after the last locator.
Behavior — trigger. The jump is quantized to the global launch quantization.
Remote control — MIDI or key mapping. Ableton/Manual/06/03 Launching the Arrangement with Locators keeps a suggested key for it.

Behavior — trigger. The jump is quantized to the global launch quantization.
Remote control — MIDI or key mapping. Ableton/Manual/06/03 Launching the Arrangement with Locators keeps a suggested key for it.

Adds a locator to the Ableton/Live/UI/Arrangement View/Scrub Area at the play position during playback or recording; with the transport stopped, at the insert marker or the start of the time selection.
When a locator is selected, the button becomes the Delete Locator button.
Behavior — trigger. New locators are quantized to the global launch quantization.
Remote control — MIDI or key mapping. Ableton/Manual/06/03 Launching the Arrangement with Locators keeps a suggested key for it.

The flashing blue marker on a track where playback starts. Click in a track to move it; double-click the Ableton/Live/UI/Control Bar/Button/Stop or press Home (Win) / Fn+Left (Mac) to return it to the start.
Moves with the Ableton/Live/UI/Control Bar/Field/Arrangement Position.
Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/03 Transport and Playback · 6.3 Transport and Playback
Marks the section the Arrangement loop repeats. Drag an edge to move the start or end, or drag the bar to move the loop without changing its length.
Arrow keys nudge it by the grid or by its own length; Cmd (Mac) / Ctrl (Win) with the arrow keys shortens, lengthens, doubles or halves it.
Its start and end are also the punch-in and punch-out points: Ableton/Live/UI/Control Bar/Switch/Punch-In, Ableton/Live/UI/Control Bar/Switch/Punch-Out.
Turned on with the Ableton/Live/UI/Control Bar/Toggle/Arrangement Loop.
Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/06 The Arrangement Loop · 6.6 The Arrangement Loop
Changes the time signature from its position onward. Markers sit just below the beat-time ruler and are hidden when a Set has no meter changes.
Insert one with Insert Time Signature Change in the Create menu or the scrub area's context menu; edit it with Cmd+R (Mac) / Ctrl+R (Win).
Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/05 Time Signature Changes · 6.5 Time Signature Changes
The strip above the tracks: click anywhere to start playback from that point, or hold the mouse button to loop a short section at the global launch quantization.
Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/03 Transport and Playback · 6.3 Transport and Playback
A launchable marker in the scrub area. Click it to jump to it; drag it or use the arrow keys to move it; rename it with Cmd+R (Mac) / Ctrl+R (Win).

Added with the Ableton/Live/UI/Arrangement View/Button/Set Locator and reached with the Ableton/Live/UI/Arrangement View/Button/Previous Locator and Ableton/Live/UI/Arrangement View/Button/Next Locator.
Its context menu offers Loop to Next Locator and Set Song Start Time Here.
Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/04 Launching the Arrangement with Locators · 6.4 Launching the Arrangement with Locators
Enlarges the waveform display in audio clips without changing clip gain. The zoom applies to all audio tracks in the Arrangement and to new clips as they are recorded.
Shows time in minutes-seconds-milliseconds; drag in it to scroll left or right.
Locks automation envelopes to the song position rather than to clips, so clips can move without moving their automation.
The bar across the top of Live's window with the transport, tempo, loop and view controls. The controls below are the ones the Arrangement View uses.

Records into the Arrangement: armed tracks record their input as new clips, and Session clips launched, their property changes, and mixer and device automation are written to the Arrangement.
Press it again or stop playback to finish recording.

With Start Playback with Record on in the Record, Warp & Launch Settings, recording starts when the button is pressed; otherwise it waits for Play or a launched Session clip. Shift-click does the opposite.
Remote control — MIDI or key mapping. Launchpad/Custom/Mode/1 Arrangement maps a Launchpad pad to it.

Enables recording of mixer and device parameter changes as automation in Session clips or Arrangement tracks, and tempo changes in the Arrangement.
Behavior — toggle: on enables automation recording; off disables automation recording.

In Arrangement View, enable Automation Arm and start Ableton/Live/UI/Control Bar/Button/Arrangement Record. Manual changes to tempo, mixer and device parameters are recorded on all tracks; individual track arming is unnecessary for automation.

In Session View, enable Automation Arm, arm the tracks and start Session Record to record mixer and device changes into clips. Setting Record Session automation in to All Tracks records into all playing clips, regardless of track arming.
